evidence.excerpt:
Userrequestsserveasresearchspecificationsfordeepresearch
agents, shaping what evidence to seek and how to synthesize
it. In personalized deep research, these specifications must
additionally reflect user goals, constraints, preferences, and
evaluation criteria. User context can be incorporated either
within the deep research pipeline or into the research specifi-
cationprovidedasitsinput.Wefocusonthelatter,refiningthe
user request into a personalized research specification before
passing it to an unchanged deep research agent. This requires
resolving three coupled decisions: which framing factors are
relevant, whether the available user context sufficiently sup-
ports them, and whether to retrieve user memory, ask the
user, or stop and refine the query. For training, G-STEER
organizes framing factors as elicitation targets in an Intent
Elicitation Graph that captures their dependencies.

Evaluation.We evaluate each refined query against ref-
erence elicitation targets using precision, recall, and F1.
Because these metrics treat all targets equally, we also re-
port weighted coverage (WCov), the normalized sum of
PDR-Bench rubric-derived importance weights over cov-
ered targets, and E-WCov, its restriction to essential tar-
gets. GPT-5.4 extracts user-specific framing factors from
each refined query, and the extracted factors and reference
targets are encoded withsentence-transformers/
all-mpnet-base-v2(Reimers and Gurevych 2019;
Song et al. 2020). A target is covered if its maximum co-
sine similarity to an extracted factor is at least 0.55.

based memory store, motivating future work with human
interaction and richer memory systems. Overall, effective
personalized research requires identifying relevant context,
grounding it appropriately, and knowing when to stop.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream report personalization and quality were measured on two fixed execution platforms, OpenAI Deep Research and OAgents, using the PDR-Bench P/Q protocol, and G-STEER achieved the highest overall P-score within both settings.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Intrinsic coverage metrics use GPT-5.4 to extract framing factors from refined queries and all-mpnet-base-v2 cosine matching against the same reference targets; downstream P/Q scores use GPT-5.4 rubric scoring of reports from two fixed DRAs.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: GRPO reward anchors are the offline elicitation targets, with coverage scored by all-mpnet-base-v2 embedding similarity between target descriptions and covered slots, plus rule-based acquisition and behavioral penalties.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported experimental results substantiate the claims, showing that G-STEER improves weighted target coverage and downstream personalization alignment while substantially decreasing clarification question burden compared to strong baselines.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation combines intrinsic target coverage metrics on PDR-Bench across seen and unseen splits with extrinsic downstream report evaluation using two deep research agents (OpenAI Deep Research and OAgents) under established PQR protocols.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream research report personalization and quality were evaluated across two independent execution platforms (commercial black-box OpenAI Deep Research and open-source OAgents) evaluated on GPT-5.4 PQR rubric scoring.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Intrinsic precision, recall, and weighted coverage metrics scored via GPT-5.4 target extraction, as well as extrinsic downstream report evaluation using multi-round GPT-5.4 scoring under the PDR-Bench PQR protocol.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Target-anchored alignment reward using embedding cosine similarity (all-mpnet-base-v2) to match covered slots to offline elicitation targets, combined with rule-based acquisition and behavioral penalties during GRPO.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including reliance on simulated user interactions, reliance on LLM-based target extraction, and the use of simple retrieval-based memory rather than complex human dynamic studies.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the extraction of elicitation targets, graph-scaffolded trajectory construction for SFT, and GRPO reward optimization balancing semantic target coverage against action and violation costs.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a well-defined scoping and methodological formulation, backed by solid experimental controls, ablations across training stages and graph ordering, sensitivity analyses, and dual downstream DRA evaluations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents G-STEER, a framework for personalized deep research query refinement that routes evidence acquisition between memory retrieval, user clarification, and stopping using Intent Elicitation Graphs and target-anchored reinforcement learning.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a well-defined scoping and methodological formulation, backed by solid experimental controls, ablations across training stages and graph ordering, sensitivity analyses, and dual downstream DRA evaluations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including reliance on simulated user interactions, reliance on LLM-based target extraction, and the use of simple retrieval-based memory rather than complex human dynamic studies.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
